actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, and in addition to the Committee on Agriculture, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

dimensions.assessment: Directly involves federal land management agencies, state, local, and Tribal governments, foundations, and relevant stakeholders.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretaries, in consultation with State, Tribal, and local governments and relevant stakeholders, shall jointly develop a strategy

dimensions.assessment: Requires strategic planning, scientific assessment, and reporting rather than direct regulatory mandates or large-scale spending programs.
dimensions.evidence: jointly develop a strategy to increase the use of aquatic restoration and conservation activities as a method of wildfire risk mitigation

dimensions.assessment: Does not state specific funding amounts or appropriations, only authorizes cooperative agreements with specific foundations and Indian Tribes.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretaries may enter into a cooperative agreement or mutual benefit agreement with the following

dimensions.assessment: Directs a federal interagency strategy integrating multiple existing statutory authorities and land management plans.
dimensions.evidence: identify opportunities to improve the effectiveness of wildfire risk mitigation... through the increased use of aquatic restoration and conservation activities

dimensions.assessment: Requires a one-year initial strategy development and ongoing integration into long-term land management activities.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretaries... shall jointly develop a strategy

missing_information: No funding levels or appropriations are specified in the text.
Exact acreage or geographic extent of 'covered lands' subject to the strategy is not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates that the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior jointly develop a strategy to increase aquatic restoration and conservation activities for wildfire risk mitigation and post-fire recovery on federal lands, submit reports, and optionally enter into cooperative agreements.
